| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.1$ | $0$ | $0$ |
| $X=1$ | $0$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ |

Find the conditional probability mass function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)$ given that the random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above.
question.worked_solution:
The conditional probability mass function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is defined as

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=P(X=x\,|\,Y=y).
$$

Therefore, we're required to compute the following set of conditional probabilities:

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)=P(X=x\,|\,Y=1)
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(X=x\,|\,Y=1)=\frac{P(X=x,Y=1)}{P(Y=1)}=\frac{f(x,1)}{{f}_{Y}(1)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distributions for $X$ and $Y$ correspond to the row and column totals, respectively. So, let's compute these:

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | ${f}_{X}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.1$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=1$ | $0$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ | $0.6$ |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.2$ | $0.4$ | $0.4$ | $1$ |

Therefore, for $x\in \{0,1,2\},$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,|\,Y=1) & =\frac{f(0,1)}{{f}_{Y}(1)}=\frac{0}{0.4}=0 \\ P(X=1\,|\,Y=1) & =\frac{f(1,1)}{{f}_{Y}(1)}=\frac{0.2}{0.4}=0.5 \\ P(X=2\,|\,Y=1) & =\frac{f(2,1)}{{f}_{Y}(1)}=\frac{0.2}{0.4}=0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the conditional probability mass function can be represented by the following table:   

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)$ | $0$ | $0.5$ | $0.5$ |
